I farm 34.5 mu, that is a lot of land for two people. My son comes back to help at busy times but mostly it is me. I will do what I did last year because last year was not bad.

I split my land like this. About 20 mu I do wheat then maize on the same ground, like always — the ground does not rest. The other 14.5 mu I keep for cotton because the price has been alright and I have grown cotton on that piece for many years, that soil suits it.

For the wheat I sow in October after the maize comes off. I buy the seed from the dealer in town, the same kind my neighbor Old Wang uses, he gets good heads. Before sowing I spread 1 bag of compound fertilizer per mu, that is 50 jin — no wait, 1 bag is 50 kg, so about 40 kg per mu I put down, maybe a bit more on the thin spots. Then in spring when the wheat turns green I scatter urea, half a bag per mu, 25 kg or so. I water the wheat 3 times — once before winter so it does not freeze dry, once at greening, once when the head is filling. I spray 2 times, once for weeds in spring, once when I see aphids on the leaves. I run the small tractor with the rotary to work the ground before sowing. Usually I get about 900 jin per mu, that is 450 kg.

Summer maize I drill straight after wheat harvest, no plowing, just the seeder behind the tractor. I put compound fertilizer with the seed, 1 bag per mu again. When the maize is waist-high I side-dress urea, half a bag. I water maybe twice if the rain is poor, once if rain comes. Spray once for the borer when I see the holes. Yield about 1100 jin, 550 kg.

Cotton is more work. The ground gets plowed proper in spring. I put 1 and a half bags of compound per mu before sowing, and topdress urea twice — at squaring and at blooming, half a bag each time. Cotton drinks a lot, I water 3 times from the well. Bollworm and aphids come every year so I spray 5 times, sometimes 6 if they are bad. Seed cotton I get about 500 jin per mu, 250 kg.
